claims.text: Adding a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion to CoCrFeNi will lower its coefficient of friction from 25 °C to 800 °C relative to unreinforced CoCrFeNi.
Adding a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion to CoCrFeNi will reduce its wear rate from 25 °C to 800 °C relative to unreinforced CoCrFeNi.
Nanoscale Y2O3 will refine the CoCrFeNi microstructure.
Nanoscale Y2O3 will pin dislocations in CoCrFeNi at low temperatures.
Microstructural refinement and dislocation pinning caused by Y2O3 will lower low-temperature friction and wear.
Y2O3 particles will remain stable dispersion reinforcements at low temperatures.
Y2O3 particles will act as nucleation sites for an oxide tribofilm at elevated temperatures.
Y2O3 particles will stabilize a continuous, low-shear oxide tribofilm at elevated temperatures.
The high-temperature tribofilm will contain mixed oxides of Co, Cr, and Fe.
The Y2O3-assisted oxide film will be protective and lubricious.
The Y2O3-assisted oxide film will mitigate adhesive wear at high temperatures.
The Y2O3 composite will show particularly notable tribological improvement at 800 °C because of the lubricious oxide layer.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits elevated friction and wear, especially at high temperatures.
The high-temperature performance degradation of baseline CoCrFeNi results from inadequate high-temperature tribological stability.
Improved tribological behavior requires the Y2O3 particles to be uniformly dispersed.
High-energy ball milling followed by hot isostatic pressing and advanced mixing can produce the targeted uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion.
